_note: Coordinates use the current IAU standard (positive-east longitude). Landing sites use the Davies & Colvin (1987/2000) precise values, cross-referenced against NASA history office data.

landmarks.name: Apollo 11
landmarks.note: Tranquility Base — first crewed Moon landing, July 20, 1969.

landmarks.name: Apollo 12
landmarks.note: Second crewed landing, in the Ocean of Storms, November 1969.

landmarks.name: Apollo 14
landmarks.note: Fra Mauro highlands, February 1971.

landmarks.name: Apollo 15
landmarks.note: Hadley–Apennine — first mission with the Lunar Roving Vehicle.

landmarks.name: Apollo 16
landmarks.note: Descartes Highlands, April 1972.

landmarks.name: Apollo 17
landmarks.note: Taurus–Littrow — the last crewed Moon landing, December 1972.

landmarks.name: Tycho
landmarks.note: Young crater with the Moon's most spectacular ray system, radiating over a thousand kilometers.

landmarks.name: Copernicus
landmarks.note: Nicknamed the 'Monarch of the Moon' — one of the most photographed craters, with a sharply terraced rim.

landmarks.name: Aristarchus
landmarks.note: The brightest large feature on the Moon — visible even by earthshine.

landmarks.name: Plato
landmarks.note: A lava-flooded crater with a smooth, dark floor that stands out from its surroundings.

landmarks.name: Kepler
landmarks.note: A small, young crater with an extensive bright ray system.

landmarks.name: Grimaldi
landmarks.note: One of the darkest features on the Moon, near the western limb.

landmarks.name: Aristoteles
landmarks.note: A large crater on the southern edge of Mare Frigoris.

landmarks.name: Aristillus
landmarks.note: A prominent, sharply-defined crater in eastern Mare Imbrium.

landmarks.name: Montes Apenninus
landmarks.note: The Moon's grandest mountain range — a remnant of the Imbrium impact, towering over the Apollo 15 site.

landmarks.name: Rima Hadley
landmarks.note: A sinuous canyon explored on foot and by rover during Apollo 15.

landmarks.name: Mare Imbrium
landmarks.note: The 'Sea of Rains' — the Moon's largest and most dominant nearside basin.

landmarks.name: Mare Serenitatis
landmarks.note: The 'Sea of Serenity,' bordered by the Apennine and Caucasus mountains.

landmarks.name: Mare Crisium
landmarks.note: The 'Sea of Crises' — a strikingly round, isolated dark patch near the eastern limb.

landmarks.name: Mare Tranquillitatis
landmarks.note: The 'Sea of Tranquility' — where Apollo 11 first landed.

landmarks.name: Oceanus Procellarum
landmarks.note: The 'Ocean of Storms' — the largest lunar mare, covering over 10% of the Moon's surface.

landmarks.name: Sinus Iridum
landmarks.note: The 'Bay of Rainbows' — a striking semicircular bay opening onto Mare Imbrium.
